issuing_body: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
covered_actors: Providers of AI systems (including high-risk AI systems, generative AI systems, and general-purpose AI models and systems)
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), including start-ups, and small mid-cap enterprises (SMCs)
Providers and same-undertaking deployers of AI systems constituting or integrated into very large online platforms (VLOPs) and very large online search engines (VLOSEs)
Third parties supplying AI systems, AI models, tools, services, components, or processes integrated into high-risk AI systems
Product manufacturers covered by Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I (including machinery and civil aviation)
Conformity assessment bodies and notified bodies
Public authorities and Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
prohibited_practices: Placing on the market, putting into service, or use of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic images, videos, audio, or similar material of an identifiable natural person's intimate parts or sexually explicit activities without that person's freely-given, specific, informed, unambiguous, and explicit consent (where intended or where reasonably foreseeable and reproducible without reasonable and adequate technical safety measures and safeguards for providers, or used for that purpose by deployers)

Placing on the market, putting into service, or use of an AI system that generates or manipulates child sexual abuse material or performance within the meaning of Article 2, points (c) and (e), of Directive 2011/93/EU, except where a 'without right' defence applies under national law (under the same provider and deployer conditions)

evidence.quote: the deployer may, when conducting the fundamental rights impact assessment referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, include cross-references to the relevant sections of that data protection impact assessment or include relevant parts thereof in the fundamental rights impact assessment.

Furthermore, a provider applying Article 6(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 remains obligated to document its assessment before that AI system is placed on the market or put into service. National competent authorities should be able to request that assessment.

Providers or prospective providers may conduct testing of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III or covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I in real world conditions at any time before the placing on the market or the putting into service of the high-risk AI system on their own or in partnership with one or more deployers or prospective deployers.

The AI Office shall be responsible for conformity assessments and tests of AI systems referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article that are classified as high-risk and subject to a third-party conformity assessment pursuant to Article 43 before such AI systems are placed on the market or put into service.

By way of derogation from Article 73, providers of high-risk AI systems subject to the competence of the AI Office pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article shall report any serious incidents to the AI Office.

That technical documentation shall be drawn up in such a way as to demonstrate that the high-risk AI system complies with the requirements set out in this Section and to provide national competent authorities and notified bodies with the necessary information in a clear and comprehensive form to assess the compliance of the AI system with those requirements.
The post-market monitoring system shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan. The post-market monitoring plan shall be part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV.

For the purposes of that conformity assessment, notified bodies which have been notified under the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I shall have the power to assess the conformity of high-risk AI systems with the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter

The Commission shall entrust the performance of those tests or assessments to notified bodies designated in accordance with this Regulation, in which case the notified body shall act on behalf of the Commission.

(c)
the special categories of personal data are subject to measures to ensure that the personal data processed are secured and protected, subject to suitable safeguards, including strict controls and documentation of the access, to avoid misuse and to ensure that only authorised persons have access to those personal data with appropriate confidentiality obligations;

Where high-risk AI systems fall within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 and the conditions laid down in Article 12(1) of that Regulation are fulfilled, such systems shall be deemed to comply with the cybersecurity requirements set out in Article 15 of this Regulation.

The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection, marking and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content.

Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026.

To streamline compliance and reduce associated costs, the registration of AI systems referred to in Article 6(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 in the EU database pursuant to Article 49(2) of that Regulation should be simplified by streamlining the content required under Annex VIII to that Regulation.

High-risk AI systems which make use of techniques involving the training of AI models with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria referred to in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of this Article and in Article 4a(1) whenever such data sets are used.

To the extent strictly necessary to ensure bias detection and correction in relation to high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 10(2), points (f) and (g), of this Regulation, providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons.
This paragraph shall not apply to third parties making accessible to the public tools, services, processes, or components, other than general-purpose AI models, under a free and open-source licence.

A decision adopted pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article may be accompanied by the imposition of penalties in accordance with Article 99(3) to (7), which provisions shall apply
mutatis mutandis
to the AI Office in the execution of its supervision and enforcement tasks referred to in Article 75(1).

Those penalty payments shall be effective and proportionate, and, where applicable, shall not exceed 5 % of the average daily income or worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year per day, calculated from the date appointed by the decision.

Before taking a decision that would have the effect of prohibiting or restricting the AI system being made available or put into service on a national market, or a decision to withdraw or recall the AI system from such market, the AI Office shall, without undue delay, notify the market surveillance authority competent for that market of its intention to take such a decision.

(bb)
the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that generates or manipulates material or performance within the meaning of Article 2, points (c) and (e), of Directive 2011/93/EU, except where a “without right” defence applies under national law;

When exercising its tasks of supervision and enforcement laid down in Article 75(1) of this Regulation, the AI Office shall have all the powers of a market surveillance authority provided for in this Section and in Article 14(4) and Article 16(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.

In order to carry out the tasks assigned to it under this Section, the AI Office may conduct all necessary remote or on-site inspections pursuant to the powers laid down in Article 14(4), points (d) and (e) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Article 74(5) of this Regulation.

By way of derogation from Article 73, providers of high-risk AI systems subject to the competence of the AI Office pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article shall report any serious incidents to the AI Office.
The operator concerned shall provide the AI Office with a description of the measures it has taken to ensure compliance with the decision upon their implementation.

The Commission and the Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of the objectives of the codes of practice by the participants and their contribution to the proper application of this Regulation.

The AI Office shall publish the decisions it adopts pursuant to Articles 75b and 75c. Such publication shall state the names of the parties and the main content of the decision, including any penalties imposed.

enforcement_authorities: National competent authorities and national market surveillance authorities (including single points of contact)
National public authorities or bodies supervising or enforcing Union law protecting fundamental rights
Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU)
National judicial authorities (for authorisation of on-site inspections where required under national law)
compliance_deadlines: 2026-07-27: Entry into force of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and application of Articles 102 to 110 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
2026-12-02: Application of Article 5(1)(ba)-(bb) and Article 5(1a)-(1b) prohibitions on non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material

2026-12-02: Transitional deadline for providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video, or text content placed on the market before 2 August 2026 to comply with Article 50(2) marking obligations
2027-08-01: Commission deadline to publish guidelines on practical implementation of Articles 8(2), 9(10), and 17(3) for Annex I Section A high-risk AI systems
2027-08-02: Member States to ensure at least one national AI regulatory sandbox is operational
2027-08-02: Commission deadline to adopt delegated acts under Article 2(13) specifying limitations on overlapping obligations for Annex I Section A high-risk AI systems
2027-09-02: Commission deadline to adopt guidance and a template on the post-market monitoring plan under Article 72(3)
2027-12-02: Application of Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3 (high-risk AI obligations) for AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III
2028-01-28: Deadline for notified bodies already notified under Annex I Section A Union harmonisation legislation to apply for designation under Chapter III, Section 4

2028-08-02: Application of Chapter III, Sections 1, 2, and 3 (high-risk AI obligations) for AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I, and deadline for Commission delegated acts amending Annex III to Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation) to apply
2030-08-02: Compliance deadline for providers and deployers of legacy high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities
penalties_summary: Member States must establish effective, proportionate, and dissuasive penalties and enforcement measures (including administrative fines, warnings, and non-monetary measures), taking into account the interests and economic viability of SMEs (including start-ups) and SMCs; for SMCs, fines under Article 99(4) and (5) are capped at the lower of the applicable percentage or fixed amount. Infringements of Article 25(2) and (4) are added to Article 99(4) administrative fines. For AI systems under its exclusive competence, the AI Office may adopt non-compliance decisions, impose administrative fines under Article 99(3)-(7) (including for non-compliance with investigatory/corrective orders, binding commitments, or supplying incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information), impose periodic penalty payments up to 5% of average daily income or worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year per day, and reclaim full supervision and enforcement costs from non-compliant operators, subject to a five-year limitation period and CJEU review.
implementation_notes: Adopted on 8 July 2026 and published on 24 July 2026, this Digital Omnibus on AI amends Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (EU AI Act), Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (civil aviation), and Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (machinery) to simplify implementation and address delays in harmonised standards and national governance. Key changes include postponing high-risk AI obligations to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I), extending SME compliance reliefs to SMCs and simplified QMS to all SMEs, refining the 'safety component' definition, revising Article 4 AI literacy to a support duty, broadening Article 4a special-category personal data processing for bias detection and correction, adding Article 5 prohibitions on non-consensual intimate material and CSAM, codifying detailed AI Office supervisory, investigatory, commitment, conformity assessment, and fining powers over GPAI-based systems and VLOP/VLOSE systems (Articles 75-75d), moving the Machinery Regulation from Annex I Section A to Section B, expanding real-world testing to Annex I systems, and adding Annex XIV notified-body designation codes.
